<a id="import-and-export"></a>

# Import and Export

Two forms exist. `dump` copies the book container byte for byte and `restore` writes it back into a store; the restored manifest keeps its version, so an older artifact needs `migrate apply` before authoring. `export` writes a reviewable text directory (`export.json`, `manifest.json`, `blocks/`, `layouts/`) and `import` creates a new book from it. The text form is the only import source: `DocEngine` books, `library import`, `book adopt` and legacy stores are not read.

The sidecar names the format, the book, the versions and one SHA-256 per member. `export --check` compares the directory and the book and reports missing, extra and changed members; `import --verify` enforces the hashes, while a hand-edited export needs no flag and is validated on import. Import allocates one fresh ID range and remaps every node, block, region, block-meta entry and layout member; an inline `[[id:N]]` is remapped, and a reference that resolves nowhere fails with `import.unresolved-ref` — never a dangling link. Cross-book links survive only when the target book is registered with the same IDs.

Import is all-or-nothing across the container, the registry and the ID ledger: a failure restores the ledger and the registry and removes the container. `restore --force` replaces a registered book behind a book-level rollback point and refuses an ID collision with another book. Import never overwrites. The loss list is the registry entry, the book ID unless `--as` matches, the ledger position, the derived state and inbound links from other books.
